content: Running aspire agent init for real, instead of trusting the documentation research from trail ba0c2c65, showed the previous cycle's pmcro-aspire skill (trail 3a9ec041) was wrong about its core mechanism: no MCP server gets registered; the real integration is the Aspire CLI's local backchannel via CLI commands, documented by the skill files aspire agent init installs. Corrected every asset in the skill to match, including a safety-relevant correction (environment values are NOT excluded, contrary to what v0.1.0 claimed). Also surfaced that this session's whole AppHost lifecycle pattern (dotnet run + manual process killing) is a documented anti-pattern with a real GitHub issue behind it; verified the correct replacement (aspire start/wait/stop) live and it worked cleanly, including auto-recovering a stray instance with no manual intervention. Filed a next_seed to adopt this pattern going forward rather than let this cycle's finding go unused.

next_seed.summary: This session used 'dotnet run --project <AppHost>' plus manual Stop-Process hunting for every AppHost start/stop this whole session, which aspire-orchestration's own skill (installed this cycle) documents as a compliance violation causing exactly the MSB3027/MSB3021 file-lock errors hit repeatedly. Adopt 'aspire start'/'aspire wait <resource>'/'aspire stop' as the standard pattern for all future live-verification work in this repo, and consider whether any earlier trail's evidence should note this as a known deviation.
